mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand offset by a nascent housing recovery, resulting in muted S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with housing recovery
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is less than -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depress corporate earnings expectations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) while consumer spending (GDPC1) remains flat signals a supply-side contraction without demand offset, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND GDPC1 monthly change between -0.2% and +0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in the federal funds rate below 1% signals an emergency easing episode, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 1% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is less than +0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 2% in real personal income (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) signals a savings glut, which reduces near-term consumption-driven corporate revenues and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change >= 2% AND RSAFS monthly change < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of at least 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) accompanied by a concurrent increase of at least 0.5% in average hourly earnings (not available, so use PAYEMS as proxy for tight labor market) signals a tight labor market, which elevates input costs and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change <= -0.3pp AND PAYEMS monthly change >= 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 4% for three consecutive quarters signals a strong demand expansion, which supports corporate earnings momentum and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annualized growth > 4% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is less than +1%.
